items.summary: fix: resume configured fallback after interrupted attempts (#188672) ` or `Related: #` line below this comment. Required PR title: type: user-facing description Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity: fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore. For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger: fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments Avoid implementation details such as: fix: add null check to task query **MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed. --> ## What Problem This Solves when ." For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug. Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause. --> Fixes: a configured fallback can report the backup model yet send no backup request and return a silent result after an interrupted primary attempt. ## User Impact ." Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence. For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit. Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here. --> User impact: configured fallback attempts can continue the unanswered turn after operational model-switch notices and owner-classified timeouts. ## Why This Change Was Made ; include technical detail only when it explains behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in . --> The existing persisted-turn replay owner now treats a model-fallback notice as operational bookkeeping rather than a completed answer. It also receives the existing fallback reason so a same-run timeout abort can continue. Direct and historical aborts and current source, target, writer, lifecycle, and cancellation checks retain their existing boundaries. ## Evidence , keeping the useful evidence summary visible. --> - Original reply, cron strictness, timeout, and streamed-recovery boundaries (F1–F4) have qualified supporting proof. The original cron timeout reproduced the silent, primary-only failure on the base and passed with the repair. Final affected routes exercised real scripted HTTP provider requests under Node 24 and checksum-pinned OpenClaw Bun. - 58 existing replay-owner case instances passed across bounded selections, including current-authority and direct/historical-abort negatives; this was not a single uninterrupted full-file run. All 14 prompt-prefix stability cases passed. No tests or assertions changed. - Focused strict typecheck, source-backed lint, formatting, unchanged test-line ratchet, and diff checks passed. Independent local autoreview of the complete two-file snapshot against `edeae71308d8` was scoped-clean at P0–P2 with no findings. The committed source is byte-identical to that reviewed snapshot. - The separate original Gateway boundaries F5 (recovered terminal content/notice prefix), F6 (the 180-second timeout), and F7 (spawned/hidden/direct ladders) were not executed successfully through setup and remain UNKNOWN. F6's reached stage and timeout cause remain independently unknown. These are not repair passes or a claim that all seven failure families share a cause. Public model listing and external provider/SDK availability are also unverified; no live paid provider was used. - Repository PR CI supplies the pending broad proof for this head. Requested by @steipete ## Work sessions [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069) Co-authored-by: steipete

items.title: improve: avoid unnecessary transcript compression projections (#188655)
items.summary: improve: avoid unnecessary transcript compression projections (#188655) Skip the native transcript metadata SELECT when the compressed frame, prepared report, and encoder-derived minimum cannot satisfy the existing savings threshold. Preserve byte-identical transcript/provider data, model-selection facts, restart delivery, and PostgreSQL behavior. Addresses the redundant payload work from #185730 and #184702. Synthetic Gateway proof reduces ordinary warm turns from 48 to 45 SQL statements, with 13 worker requests and zero MAIN SQL unchanged; all fourteen turns and restart flows pass. The first sealed-history fingerprint from #186046 remains required. Validated with payload and prompt-prefix tests, 48 byte-equivalent variants, two isolated code reviews plus a type-correction delta review, and exact-head CI/PostgreSQL conformance.
